Theme

School & learning

historical adjective

of history; in recorded history

also historically, historic (of history), in recorded history, historian

classical

Cic. Brut. 286: nōn tam historicō quam ōrātōriō genere
Cic. Mur. 16: hominēs litterātī et historicī (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 328 (historian)
Traupman 328

historicus, historica, historicum

Declension on Wiktionary

of history, historical; (as a noun) a historian

Of history and of writing it: genus historicum, the historians’ style; fidēs historica, a historian’s credibility (Ov. Am. 3.12.42); of people, versed in history. As a noun, a historian (Cic. Top. 78; Quint.).

Other words

  • post hominum memoriam — in all recorded history, within human memory

    phrase · also used · classical · Cic. Cat. 1.16

    Cicero’s way of saying “for the first time in history”; nostrā memoriā is “in our time” (Lewis & Short, s.v. memoria).

  • historicē — historically, as a historian would

    adverb · also used · classical · Plin. Ep. 2.5.5: nōn historicē tantum, sed prope poēticē (Lewis & Short)

Examples

  • et eārum rērum historiam quae erant Athēnīs ipsīus aetāte gestae nōn tam historicō quam ōrātōriō genere perscrīpsit.

    and he wrote the history of what had happened at Athens in his own lifetime in a style less historical than oratorical.Cic. Brut. 286

  • sī hoc post hominum memoriam contigit nēminī

    if this has happened to no one in all recorded historyCic. Cat. 1.16

See also history, researcher.
